title: botai course binding
description: What was accepted for one installed course, and which snapshot that acceptance refers to. The binding is what makes a course authoritative: without it the agent has files, not a policy. It never points at an editable working file — accepted_* are hashes of copies taken under .botai/accepted/, so editing botai/course.json in a student branch does not change what governs help.

slug.description: The directory name under courses/. For a legacy course whose directory is not a valid new slug, this is the safe identifier and legacy_path carries the real directory.

legacy_path.description: The original Cyrillic/underscore directory name, when slug != the on-disk name. The directory is never renamed automatically: renaming would break the paths a student already has.

repository_root.description: Verified path under courses/. A course is one directory, never a path that climbs out of the workspace.

source_url.description: Where the course came from, with any embedded credentials stripped. null for a course created locally.

teaching_remote.description: The remote course updates come from (usually upstream, or origin when the student did not fork).

contribution_remote.description: The student's fork, when there is one. A fork and the course source are two different roles, not a substitute for each other.

acceptance_kind.description: How acceptance came about. This is provenance, not a cryptographic proof that the teacher approved it.

assessment_kinds.description: Assessment values actually present in the accepted contract, so a caller can tell 'the course declares nothing graded' from 'the graded list was never read'.

material_snapshot.description: Where the accepted revision's readable material was snapshotted, relative to the workspace. Lessons are read from the snapshot, not from the working tree: otherwise an unnoticed edit changes the text the accepted contract refers to.
